label: CSS
description: Selectors, specificity, the cascade, layout with Flexbox and Grid, responsive units and modern CSS features.

questions.title: With `box-sizing: border-box`, what does `width: 200px` mean?
questions.prompt: With `box-sizing: border-box`, what does `width: 200px` mean?

options.text: The content box is 200px and padding plus border are added on top
The total box — content, padding and border together — is 200px

questions.explanation: `border-box` includes padding and border inside the declared width, which is why most resets apply it globally. With the default `content-box` the element grows past 200px.

questions.title: Which selector wins between `.card .title` and `#main .title`?
questions.prompt: Which selector wins between `.card .title` and `#main .title`?

options.text: `.card .title`, because two classes beat one class
`#main .title`, because an ID contributes more specificity than any number of classes
Whichever appears later in the stylesheet
They tie and the browser picks one at random

questions.explanation: Specificity compares (ids, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements) column by column. `#main .title` is (1,1,0) versus (0,2,0), so the ID wins before source order is considered.

questions.title: Which properties are inherited by child elements by default?
questions.prompt: Which properties are inherited by child elements by default?
questions.explanation: Typography properties inherit so a single `body` rule styles the page; box model and layout properties do not, which is why they must be set per element.

questions.title: Why is `1rem` usually preferred over `1em` for component spacing?
questions.prompt: Why is `1rem` usually preferred over `1em` for component spacing?

options.text: `rem` is relative to the root font size, so values stay predictable instead of compounding through nested `em` contexts
`em` is not a valid CSS unit

questions.explanation: `rem` resolves against the root element's font size while `em` resolves against the element's own font size, so nested components compound. Both respect the user's font-size setting.

questions.title: In a flex container, what does `flex: 1` set on an item?
questions.prompt: In a flex container, what does `flex: 1` set on an item?

options.text: `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0%` — the item absorbs free space equally
It centres the item along the cross axis

questions.explanation: The shorthand expands to `1 1 0%`, so items share leftover space after their own content needs are met. Centring on the cross axis is `align-items`, not `flex`.

questions.title: Which declaration makes a responsive grid of cards with a minimum width of 240px that grows to fill the row?
questions.prompt: Which declaration makes a responsive grid of cards with a minimum width of 240px that grows to fill the row?

options.text: `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap` with `width: 240px` on each card

questions.explanation: `auto-fill` creates as many 240px-or-wider tracks as fit, so no media queries are needed. A fixed `repeat(3, ...)` stays three columns on every screen.

questions.title: A badge must sit at the top-right corner of its parent card. What is required?
questions.prompt: A badge must sit at the top-right corner of its parent card. What is required?

options.text: `position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0` on the badge and `position: relative` on the card

questions.explanation: Absolutely positioned elements resolve against the nearest positioned ancestor, so the card needs `position: relative`. `fixed` attaches to the viewport and `sticky` is for scroll behaviour.

questions.title: Why does `@media (max-width: 767px)` avoid the classic breakpoint overlap bug?
questions.prompt: Why does `@media (max-width: 767px)` avoid the classic breakpoint overlap bug?

options.text: Because fractional device widths are impossible, so `max-width: 767px` and `min-width: 768px` cannot both match
Because media queries only support integers
Because `max-width` is evaluated in device pixels rather than CSS pixels
It does not — overlap must be solved with `!important`

questions.explanation: Using `max-width: 767.98px` (or the integer trick) keeps mobile and desktop rules mutually exclusive; `max-width: 768px` plus `min-width: 768px` would both match at exactly 768px.

questions.title: A hover animation janks the layout. Which property pair keeps it on the compositor?
questions.prompt: A hover animation janks the layout. Which property pair keeps it on the compositor?
questions.explanation: `transform` and `opacity` can be handled by the compositor thread without re-running layout or paint, so they animate at full frame rate. Geometry properties trigger layout on every frame.

questions.title: What happens when a `var()` reference points at an undefined custom property and no fallback is given?
questions.prompt: What happens when a `var()` reference points at an undefined custom property and no fallback is given?

options.text: The declaration is invalid at computed-value time, so the property falls back to its inherited or initial value
The browser treats it as an empty string and keeps the layout
The rule is dropped at parse time like a normal syntax error
It inherits the value from the nearest sibling

questions.explanation: Custom properties are resolved at computed-value time, so a missing variable makes the declaration "invalid at computed-value time" — the property becomes `unset`, not a parse error. `var(--x, fallback)` avoids it.

questions.title: What specificity do these rules carry: `.btn.primary` vs `#submit`?
questions.prompt: What specificity do these rules carry: `.btn.primary` vs `#submit`?

options.text: (1,0,0) beats (0,2,0) — an id outweighs any number of classes
They tie, so the later rule wins
Specificity only applies to inline styles

questions.explanation: Specificity is counted as (ids, classes, elements): `.btn.primary` is (0,2,0) and `#submit` is (1,0,0). The id wins before source order is even considered.

questions.title: Which properties do NOT inherit from a parent element by default?
questions.prompt: Which properties do NOT inherit from a parent element by default?
questions.explanation: Colour and typography inherit; box-level paint properties (border, background) belong to each element and must be restated explicitly.

questions.title: Without `box-sizing`, what does `width: 200px` describe on a bordered element?
questions.prompt: Without `box-sizing`, what does `width: 200px` describe on a bordered element?

options.text: Content only — padding and border are added on top

questions.explanation: The default `content-box` sizes the content only; padding and border grow the element past its declared width.

questions.title: What does `font-size: 2rem` resolve to on an element whose parent is 32px?
questions.prompt: What does `font-size: 2rem` resolve to on an element whose parent is 32px?

options.text: 32px — rem is relative to the html root, not the parent

questions.explanation: `rem` is always relative to the root (html) font size; `em` is the one that resolves against the parent.

questions.title: Which declaration turns a div into a flex container?
questions.prompt: Which declaration turns a div into a flex container?
questions.explanation: `display: flex` establishes the flex formatting context; `flex` and `flex-direction` are properties of its *children* / axis.

questions.title: What does the selector `article > p` match?
questions.prompt: What does the selector `article > p` match?

options.text: Every p inside article, at any depth
Only p elements that are direct children of article
The first p after an article

questions.explanation: The child combinator `>` is depth-1 only; descendants at any depth would use a space.

questions.title: What does `position: absolute` do to an element with `top: 10px`?
questions.prompt: What does `position: absolute` do to an element with `top: 10px`?

options.text: Offsets it 10px from the nearest positioned ancestor (or the page)
Moves it into the document flow

questions.explanation: Absolutely positioned boxes are offset from their nearest positioned ancestor's padding box; with none present, the initial containing block.

questions.title: Which unit is relative to the viewport width?
questions.prompt: Which unit is relative to the viewport width?
questions.explanation: `vw`/`vh` are viewport-relative (1vw = 1% of viewport width), while rem/em resolve against fonts.

questions.title: Where does `font-family: Arial` on `<body>` apply?
questions.prompt: Where does `font-family: Arial` on `<body>` apply?

options.text: To body and everything that inherits font-family

questions.explanation: font-family is an inherited property, so descendants inherit it unless they set their own value.

questions.title: What is the default value of `position` for a normal div?
questions.prompt: What is the default value of `position` for a normal div?
questions.explanation: `static` is the default: the element sits in normal flow and is not a containing block for absolutely positioned descendants.

questions.title: A child has `flex: 1`, another `flex: 2`. What differs?
questions.prompt: A child has `flex: 1`, another `flex: 2`. What differs?

options.text: Their share of free space — the second grows twice as fast once both are past their flex-basis

questions.explanation: After the flex-basis is satisfied, remaining free space is distributed in proportion to the flex-grow factor, so 2 grows faster than 1.

questions.title: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))` do?
questions.prompt: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))` do?

options.text: Fills each row with as many columns as fit, each between 200px and equal-width

questions.explanation: `auto-fill` packs as many tracks as the container allows; `minmax(200px, 1fr)` lets each track grow but never shrink below 200px — the classic responsive grid.

questions.title: What does `transition: transform 0.3s ease` animate?
questions.prompt: What does `transition: transform 0.3s ease` animate?

options.text: Only transform, for 300ms, with an ease timing function

questions.explanation: The shorthand is `property duration timing-function`; only the listed property transitions, everything else changes instantly.

questions.title: Why do media queries generally be written small→large (min-width) in a mobile-first design?
questions.prompt: Why do media queries generally be written small→large (min-width) in a mobile-first design?

options.text: Because min-width queries are faster to parse
So base styles are the mobile default and each query only *adds* rules as space grows, avoiding override fights

questions.explanation: Mobile-first means the baseline is the narrowest layout; each larger breakpoint then adds or overrides exactly what it needs.

questions.title: What happens when a custom property falls back: `var(--brand, #333)` and `--brand` is not defined?
questions.prompt: What happens when a custom property falls back: `var(--brand, #333)` and `--brand` is not defined?

options.text: The declaration is invalid at computed-value time
The browser picks a default colour
An error is logged and the rule dropped

questions.explanation: `var()`'s second argument is a fallback used when the custom property is missing or invalid — the rule survives.

questions.title: Which pair collapses vertical margins in normal flow?
questions.prompt: Which pair collapses vertical margins in normal flow?

options.text: Adjacent vertical margins of in-flow blocks collapse

questions.explanation: Block-level vertical margins in normal flow collapse into one; flex/grid items and absolutely positioned boxes never collapse margins.

questions.title: What does `:nth-child(odd)` select on a list of ten items?
questions.prompt: What does `:nth-child(odd)` select on a list of ten items?
questions.explanation: `odd` maps to positions 1, 3, 5… — the item's position among *all* siblings, not among elements of the same type.

questions.title: Which statement about `!important` is true?
questions.prompt: Which statement about `!important` is true?

options.text: It wins all specificity comparisons of normal declarations
It increases an element's specificity value
It is scoped to a media query
It only works on inherited properties

questions.explanation: A declaration marked important outranks every normal declaration regardless of specificity — which is exactly why it's a last resort.

questions.title: Why do container queries change layout design compared to media queries?
questions.prompt: Why do container queries change layout design compared to media queries?

options.text: They respond to the container's own size, so the same component adapts wherever it is placed

questions.explanation: Media queries ask 'how wide is the viewport?'; container queries ask 'how wide is my parent?' letting a component adapt independently of page layout.

questions.title: What do `gap` on a flex container and `gap` on a grid container have in common?
questions.prompt: What do `gap` on a flex container and `gap` on a grid container have in common?

options.text: They both create spacing between tracks/items without the double-margin problem

questions.explanation: `gap` works on both layout modes and places space only *between* items, avoiding the adjacent-margin collapse/space-adding issues of margins.

questions.title: Why can `all: unset` on a button still leave it looking like a link later?
questions.prompt: Why can `all: unset` on a button still leave it looking like a link later?

options.text: It does not work on form controls
unset resolves each property to its inherited or initial value — but any later rule that targets the element outranks it

questions.explanation: unset maps inherited properties to inherit and non-inherited ones to initial; the cascade order afterwards decides everything else, so specificity still rules.

questions.title: What is the effect of `min-width: 0` on a flex child that refuses to shrink?
questions.prompt: What is the effect of `min-width: 0` on a flex child that refuses to shrink?

options.text: It removes the automatic content-based minimum, letting the item shrink below its intrinsic size
It makes the child a grid item

questions.explanation: Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, so long content can block shrinking. Setting `min-width: 0` (or overflow: hidden) makes the item actually shrinkable.

questions.title: What does `grid-column: 1 / -1` do?
questions.prompt: What does `grid-column: 1 / -1` do?

options.text: Spans from column 1 to the last explicit column line

questions.explanation: Negative line numbers index the explicit grid's end lines: `-1` is the last explicit line, so the item spans the full explicit width.

questions.title: How does `position: sticky` differ from `fixed`?
questions.prompt: How does `position: sticky` differ from `fixed`?

options.text: sticky stays in normal flow until it crosses its sticky threshold, then offsets — it never leaves its container; fixed always positions against the viewport

questions.explanation: Sticky is 'relative until it sticks': it scrolls with the page and is bounded by its ancestor. Fixed is always viewport-anchored.

questions.title: What does wrapping rules in `@layer base { ... }` change?
questions.prompt: What does wrapping rules in `@layer base { ... }` change?

options.text: Layer order is compared before specificity, so an unlayered or later-layered rule can beat a higher-specificity layered one
It scopes selectors to the layer

questions.explanation: Cascade layers rank *before* specificity within the normal origin: an unlayered rule always beats a layered one, letting teams order frameworks deliberately.

questions.title: Why is `--brand: red !important;` unusual for custom properties?
questions.prompt: Why is `--brand: red !important;` unusual for custom properties?

options.text: !important is not allowed — custom property precedence is resolved purely by cascade order and scope
It has no effect on inherited values

questions.explanation: Custom properties follow normal cascade rules only; the !important keyword is invalid in their declaration grammar.

questions.title: Which property animates cheapest — and why does it matter?
questions.prompt: Which property animates cheapest — and why does it matter?

options.text: transform and opacity — the compositor can animate them without relayout/paint

questions.explanation: Top/left/width trigger layout (and paint) on every frame; transform/opacity are handled by the GPU compositor, keeping the main thread free.

questions.title: A 1600px-wide layout uses margins on a 1600px screen — the common cause?
questions.prompt: A 1600px-wide layout uses margins on a 1600px screen — the common cause?

options.text: Horizontal percentage margins summing to 100% plus content width overflowing the viewport

questions.explanation: Percentage margins are relative to the *containing block*, so left:5% + right:5% + width:100% = 110%. Classic cause of horizontal overflow.

questions.title: What specificity does an inline `style` attribute beat?
questions.prompt: What specificity does an inline `style` attribute beat?

options.text: All normal selectors; only an inline !important beats it

questions.explanation: Inline styles sit above id selectors in the cascade (like specificity (1,0,0,0)); an inline !important declaration is one of the last resorts above it.

questions.title: In a mobile-first design, why avoid `max-width` media queries as the primary structure?
questions.prompt: In a mobile-first design, why avoid `max-width` media queries as the primary structure?

options.text: They layer overrides over the desktop styles, so base rules can leak; min-width queries grow the layout additively instead

questions.explanation: max-width queries force every later rule to undo the earlier one, which compounds as breakpoints multiply; min-width keeps each addition local.
